elements.name: question1
elements.html:
Opening

 

This study is for men aged 18 to 59 years old who have mild to moderate male pattern hair loss, also known as androgenetic alopecia.

We’re testing a new potential treatment, which is being developed to help slow down or even reverse hair loss in men.
The study is being run by OliX Pharmaceuticals, with research sites across Australia including Emeritus Research in Botany.

elements.name: question13
elements.html:
About The Study Treatment

 

The study medication is a new injection-based treatment that targets the main cause of male pattern baldness, the androgen receptor, a gene that affects how hair grows on the scalp.

By reducing the activity of this gene, the treatment aims to help new hair grow and make existing hair thicker and stronger.

The study compares treatment to a placebo.


This means some participants will receive the real treatment, and others will receive placebo but neither you nor the doctor will know which one you’re getting until the study finishes.

Each treatment session involves around 10 injections in the thinning area on the top of your head. These will be done by a group of 3 needles each time and will be about 4mm in depth and take only a few minutes to complete.

elements.name: question59
elements.html:
Phase 2a:
About 9 clinic visits + 2 short phone calls total, over roughly 7 months

 

Phase 2a (Main Hair-Growth Stage)

  • Around 130 men will take part.
  • You’ll attend 9 in-person site visits over approximately 7 months (221 days).
  • You’ll receive 6 treatment sessions, each 4 weeks apart (on Days 1, 29, 57, 85, 113 and 141).
  • You’ll also have 2 quick follow-up phone calls (on Days 43 and 71).
  • The final follow-up visit is around Day 169, about 4 weeks after your last treatment.
  • Purpose: to assess hair regrowth, safety, and overall results at different doses.

elements.name: question60
elements.html:
What To Expect At Visits

 

  • You’ll come to the clinic for each visit, no overnight stays are required.
  • Some visits will include routine checks like blood pressure, heart rate, and quick questionnaires about your health and wellbeing.
  • You’ll have a tiny freckle-sized semi-permanent dot tattoo placed on your scalp early in the study, this just helps the team measure the same area each time.
  • For some visits, the hair in a small area (about 1 cm × 1 cm) will be trimmed short so the team can take high-quality photos to count hairs.
  • You’ll need to keep your hairstyle and products consistent during the study (for example, no switching shampoos or using new hair-growth products).

elements.name: question82
elements.html:
Reimbursement

Participants will receive $437 for each of the following visits:

  • Screening Visit (Visit 1)
  • Visit 3 (Day 15)
  • Visit 4 (Day 29)
  • Visit 6 (Day 57)
  • Visit 8 (Day 85)
  • Visit 9 (Day 113)
  • Visit 10 (Day 141)
  • Visit 11 (Day 169, EOS)

 

Participants will also receive $487 at Visit 2 (Day 1), and $50 at Visits 5 (Day 43) and 7 (Day 71).

 

During the study, you may also be asked to attend an Unscheduled Visit or an Early Termination Visit if required by the study doctor. If this occurs, you will be reimbursed $437 for the visit.

 

In total, participants will be reimbursed up to $4,083 if they attend all scheduled visits.

 

The study team will also advise you if you qualify for additional reimbursement related to rural travel.

All reimbursements will be transferred to your nominated bank account after each visit is completed. Please allow up to three business days for processing.

 

Please note that if you do not have the required level or severity of hair loss appropriate for this study at screening, you will not be found eligible and will not be reimbursed for the full amount.

elements.name: question90
elements.html:
Disclosure

 

Before we go any further, I want to explain exactly how the reimbursement works, so there are no surprises for you later. The reimbursement I just went through is what you'd receive if everything goes ahead as planned. That can look a bit different depending on what happens on the day. For example, if the doctor looks over your information early on and finds you're not eligible before you even get to the consent form, if you decide not to sign the consent form yourself, or if something doesn't line up with what you've told me today, you'd likely only get a partial amount, or in some cases nothing, instead of the full reimbursement.

 

That's actually a big part of why it matters that you're as accurate as possible with me right now. The doctor's early review is based on exactly what you tell me today, so the more accurate you are, the better your chances of making it all the way through screening and getting the full reimbursement.

elements.name: question14
elements.html:
I just need to ask a few quick questions about your hair loss pattern to see if you fall in the range required for this trial.

 

This study is looking for men who fall between Stage 3vertex and Stage 5 on the Norwood-Hamilton scale.


I’ll describe what each stage looks like so you can tell me what matches you best.

 

Stage 3vertex

Stage 3vertex means there is a noticeable bald spot or thinning patch on the crown of the head,
as well as some recession at the front.

So it’s not just the temples going back — there is a clear bald/thin area on top when looking from above.

 

Stage 4/4A

Stage 4 is when:

  • The front hairline has moved back further,
  • And the bald spot on the crown is bigger,

  • But there is still a strip of hair separating the front area from the crown.

     

Stage 5

Stage 5 is more advanced:

  • The bald areas at the front and the crown are larger,
  • The strip of hair between them is thinner,
  • They’re close to joining,
  • But you are not completely bald on top.

 

Please note that if you do not have the required level or severity of hair loss appropriate for this study at screening, you will not be found eligible and will not be reimbursed for the full amount.

    Having already colored hair is OK as long as they are happy to not do anything "permanent" to it.     Not exclusionary if they are happy for the above

elements.name: question27
elements.html:
Exclusionary Medications

1. Hair loss / hormone-related medications

Must not have used within the last 24 weeks (6 months):

  • Oral Minoxidil
  • Finasteride
  • Dutasteride
  • Spironolactone
  • Flutamide
  • Cyproterone acetate
  • Cimetidine
  • Ketoconazole (oral/systemic)
  • Testosterone / anabolic steroids

2. Topical hair growth treatments

Must not have used within the last 12 weeks (3 months):

  • Topical Minoxidil
  • Topical anti-androgen solutions/serums
  • PRP injections to the scalp
  • Laser/light hair growth devices (caps, combs, helmets)
  • Topical retinoids used on the scalp

3. Hair cosmeceuticals / OTC regrowth products

Must not have used within the last 2 weeks:

  • Any over-the-counter “hair regrowth/hair stimulating” product or serum

4. Medications that can cause hair loss (hypotrichosis)

Must not have used within the last 24 weeks:

  • Haloperidol
  • Methotrexate
  • Methylprednisolone
  • Prednisone
  • Lithium
  • Carbamazepine
  • Valproic acid / Divalproex
  • Heparin
  • Warfarin (Coumarin)
  • GLP-1 receptor agonists:
    • Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy)
    • Liraglutide
    • Dulaglutide
    • Tirzepatides (Mounjaro)

5. Medications that can cause excessive hair growth (hypertrichosis)

Must not have used within the last 24 weeks:

  • Cyclosporine
  • Diazoxide
  • Phenytoin
  • Psoralens
  • Phenothiazines

6. Systemic medications affecting hormones or hair

Must not have used within the last 24 weeks:

  • Beta-blockers (e.g., propranolol, metoprolol, atenolol)
  • Systemic retinoids (e.g., isotretinoin, acitretin)

7. Anti-cancer medications

Must not have used within the last 12 months:

  • Any chemotherapy / cytotoxic cancer treatment

 

8. Other

  • Dexamphetamines (ADHD medication) in last 1 month

elements.html:
Exclusionary Medical Conditions

Chronic / systemic medical conditions

  • Significant pulmonary, liver, kidney, blood, gastrointestinal, endocrine, immune, or neurological disease
  • Uncontrolled chronic health conditions (e.g., uncontrolled diabetes or hypertension)
  • Thyroid disorders (hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism) unless well-controlled and stable for ≥ 12 weeks
  • Heart disease, including:
    • History of ischemic heart disease
    • Arrhythmias
    • Prolonged QT or family history of sudden cardiac death
    • Any cardiac condition that increases risk (e.g., torsades risk factors)

Scalp / dermatological conditions

Anything that affects the scalp or could interfere with injections, examinations, or hair assessment:

  • Fungal or bacterial scalp infections
  • Seborrheic dermatitis
  • Psoriasis
  • Eczema
  • Folliculitis
  • Scalp atrophy
  • History of:
    • Alopecia areata
    • Scarring alopecia
    • Diffuse telogen effluvium
    • Other causes of active hair loss
  • Hair transplantation (any history)
  • Scalp radiation at any point in life
  • Keloid or hypertrophic scarring tendency

Recent surgery / hospitalisation / upcoming procedures

  • Major surgery or hospitalisation in the past 3 months
  • Planned surgery during the study period

Cancer and immunologic exclusions

  • Any malignant cancer in the past 5 years
    (except completely removed non-melanoma skin cancers)
  • Positive or active:
    • HIV
    • Hepatitis B
    • Hepatitis C

Unstable Psychiatric Conditions (unstable bipolar, schizophrenia)

elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: question78
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
